prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B004 to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, with a citation deliberately narrowed to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall state. Round 1 strengthened the case in the way that matters to me. Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling plus time-reversal symmetry yields a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states with no applied field. That is a computable, testable statement about band structures, and it is the kind of result that let electronic-structure theory guide which materials to look at. Molenkamp's group then observed the predicted edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells, and about two decades of transport, ARPES and materials work have not overturned the interpretation. No member contests the scientific standing of B004, and every member who prefers another candidate names it as a first or second alternative. The chair's synthesis shows the remaining disagreement is about credit boundary and overlap with 2016, not about whether the discovery is real or mature.
statement.case_against: The omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a real defect, not a technicality. Their HgTe proposal set the experimental target Molenkamp's group tested, Zhang's death means it cannot be repaired later, and the three-name cap forces the committee to leave out a decisive step. The 2016 prize also leaves a fair impression risk of returning to topology. I now think I understated both in round 1: I called the credit a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration, but it is a natural configuration only once the citation is drawn tightly, and it should be recorded openly that it is a boundary choice. B006 is the cleaner allocation and the more directly deployed result, and if the committee decides that clean attribution should outweigh conceptual reach it is a defensible prize.

responses.point: Pearce, now preferring B004, accepts the originality and stability but wants the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission stated openly in the committee record and not treated as settled.
responses.response: I accept this and withdraw the word defensible as a way of closing the question. The omission should be recorded as a boundary choice: the citation should name the Z2 prediction and the first observation, say nothing that sweeps in the HgTe proposal as if it were credited, and the record should state that the HgTe proposal and the three-dimensional work lie outside the awarded names. I would also note that your move from B002 to B004 is the same move I made on attribution grounds, since the Higgs credit problem is structurally harder than this one.

responses.point: Johansson wants the citation kept narrow to the quantum spin Hall effect and its first observation so that three-dimensional topological insulator work is not drawn into the credited set.
responses.response: I agree, and in round 1 I was too loose about three-dimensional generalisation as part of the case. Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, Hasan and Shen's ARPES work are outside what these three names can carry. My revised citation therefore names only the time-reversal-invariant (Z2) prediction and the first HgTe observation. I would keep the word topological insulator in the theory clause because that is how Kane and Mele framed it, but not extend it to materials classification in general.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B006 for clean attribution and says she would not oppose B004 if the committee accepts the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit boundary, while also raising the 2016 overlap.
responses.response: Her condition is the right one, and the answer I would give is that accepting the boundary is a decision about this citation, not a denial of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's contribution. On the 2016 overlap I still disagree that it lowers novelty much. The 2016 prize concerned topological phase transitions and Chern-type quantised Hall physics, which require broken time reversal; Z2 insulators are a different symmetry class with a different invariant. Where I do concede your point is that the clock result has the cleaner attribution, and I would be comfortable with B006 as an alternative.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B009, argues that waiting for the pairing mechanism may mean waiting indefinitely, and names B004 as his first alternative while treating the credit gap as his main reason not to rank it first.
responses.response: Your point about waiting indefinitely is fair, but the question for a discovery prize is whether the discovery is separable from the mechanism, and for B009 the prediction and the 2018 observation are, while the experimental credit rests on one name and parallel groups are outside. I value the quantitative prediction as an electronic-structure theorist, but I do not see a stronger case here than in B004, where the prediction was tested and held for two decades. I keep B009 as my second alternative and expect it to be a serious candidate in a later year.

responses.point: Kroll and Lindroth treat the 2005 and 2012 prize overlap as answerable by anchoring the B006 citation on the magic-wavelength lattice concept.
responses.response: I agree that anchoring on Katori's lattice concept answers most of the lineage objection, and I have raised it less forcefully in round 2 than in round 1. Having heard the exchange I think the lattice clock is a larger step than I credited, and your disclosure about the Hall laboratory is a matter the committee should settle separately. I still weigh conceptual reach somewhat higher, but B006 is my first alternative and I would not stand in its way.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission as a documented boundary choice and not treat it as disqualifying; I accept it but cannot say the objection is fully answered.
Whether the 2016 prize should count as an overlap, which I judge to be small because the symmetry class and mechanism differ; this remains a judgement.
How the committee weighs conceptual reach against clean attribution in the B004 versus B006 choice, which the chair identified as the main open dispute.
Whether the magic-angle graphene mechanism will settle in a way that changes B009 in the next few years.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile, and I do not recuse myself on B004, B006 or B009. My work on electronic-structure theory and magnetism is adjacent to topological band-structure physics and moire flat bands, but I have no documented personal, supervisory or institutional connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Bistritzer or Jarillo-Herrero. I note the disclosures of Kroll, Olsson and Johansson and defer to the committee on them.
